pageProps.title: Gomtang 2: The Night Twelve People Disappeared
pageProps.review: A Korean-style time-leap novel by Kim Young-tak that stands out for its fast-paced development and meticulous retrieval of foreshadowing, highly recommended as a work that breaks prejudices against Korean novels along with deep questions about utopia.
pageProps.description: A utopia built by stealing the future, cruel truth and belated regret blooming within it
pageProps.content:
## Review Like a movie director, it is fast-paced. It retrieves the 'bait' (foreshadowing) carefully piled up in volume 1 and develops the story quickly.
Many people are sacrificed to build the utopia they think of. Does ```Utopia``` really exist?
A Korean-style time-leap work, the story development is fast and the probability of the stories seems high. A book I want to recommend to many. Since this book, personal prejudices against Korean novels seem to have disappeared.
